title: Unexpected peak analysis and rightsize plan - NimbleWorks QBR
summary: Quarterly health/check-in focused on a recent unexpected traffic peak that increased token spend by ~3x for a 36-hour window. Reviewed root-cause hypotheses (promotion surge + unbounded retries), examined Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoffs and autoscaling settings, and agreed on a three-sprint rightsizing plan plus a benchmarking pilot for quantized model variants.
topics: next steps: pilot and dashboard alerts
next_steps: Redwood to share 24-hr token-by-route breakdown and raw logs for February 12-14 spike (Maya) by 2026-03-02
NimbleWorks to enable request sampling and share SDK version + retry logic snippet (Sara) by 2026-03-03
Schedule 2-hour performance benchmark: quantized 7B vs full 13B on NimbleWorks workload (Liam + Rajiv) target week of 2026-03-15
Finance sync to update monthly forecast and temporary cap for unexpected spikes (Tom) by 2026-03-05
action_items: Maya Patel | Exported per-route token spend CSV and KV-cache hit-rate summary | 2026-03-02
Liam O'Connor | Run internal bench with 4 different batching configs and provide recommendations | 2026-03-10
Sara Chen | Share retry/backoff code and traffic schedule for the February promo | 2026-03-03
Rajiv Menon | Turn on Prometheus route-level metrics in staging and enable alert rule for token rate > 2x baseline | 2026-03-01
Tom Alvarez | Propose temporary buffer in budget and approve pilot spend up to $8k | 2026-03-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27 | 15:00 PST | Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Sara (NimbleWorks), Rajiv (SRE), Elena (Product), Tom (Finance)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick QBR/incident deep-dive on that token spike in mid-Feb — I know it's been noisy, so we wanted to walk through what we saw and align on a remediation plan.
[00:18] Sara: Yeah thanks, appreciate it. we got hit by a promo and then the retry loop made things worse, so i'm hoping we can get to concrete config changes.
[00:30] Liam: I'll start with what we observed from the Redwood side — overall token volume spiked roughly 3x for ~36 hours, embeddings calls spiked about 2.5x, and we saw an increase in short-lived sessions that bypassed prefix caching. There were also a lot of small-chunk requests which prevented efficient batching.
[01:00] Rajiv: small-chunk requests = many 64-token calls rather than aggregated 512s?
[01:05] Liam: exactly. it looks like the client SDK in production had an older batching config (weird defaults), and combined with aggressive retries, the effective qps ballooned.
[01:22] Elena: To confirm: the promo drove more users, but our client changes amplified it. so it's not purely Redwood capacity — we need changes client-side too.
[01:34] Maya: right. on the platform side we had autoscale react, but because the traffic had many concurrent small requests, the KV-cache had lower hit rates and batching efficiency dropped, so p95 latency went up and token cost per logical request increased.
[01:50] Tom: From finance perspective the bill for that window was ~3x the baseline for that feature; surprised us. can Redwood break out cost by model and route so we can show execs?
[02:05] Maya: yes, i'll export per-route token spend and model mapping. we'll include hits/misses on the K-V cash — sorry K-V cash, i mean KV cache — the auto-transcription messes up :)
[02:20] (laughter)
[02:28] Sara: there's also a question of whether Dedicated or Hosted would have helped — if we'd been on Dedicated reserved pools maybe autoscaling would've behaved differently?
[02:41] Liam: Dedicated gives predictability and isolated pools, but it doesn't magically fix poor batching; it can help with tail latency and prevent noisy neighbors. for this particular event dedicated could reduce cost variance if you size pools correctly, but you'd still want client batching and retry fixes.
[03:05] Rajiv: do you have suggested autoscale/burst configs we should consider? we saw a lot of small bursts.
[03:12] Liam: yes — two immediate levers: reduce max_concurrency per host so batches fill more slowly (counterintuitive) and increase time-window for batching slightly so you get better batch assembly; also set burst capacity with a short warm-up policy so it handles short peaks without overprovisioning long-term. we'll propose exact knobs.
[03:36] Elena: you mentioned quantization — could we move to a smaller quantized variant for cost savings without too much quality hit?
[03:43] Liam: we can try 4-bit quant for the 7B family or 8-bit for 13B; recommended path is run a benchmark on your prompt set. we'll supply evaluation harness and a quick quality checklist — if latency and quality are acceptable we can plan a staged rollout.
[04:05] Sara: ok that benchmark is high priority. also, can Redwood set alerts so we get notified before costs spiral?
[04:12] Priya: yes we've got new alerting templates you can adopt — token-rate anomaly, kv-cache drop, and per-route spend threshold. we'll share the alert rules YAML.
[04:25] Tom: about billing — is there a way to put a temporary cap or a soft-limit notification before hitting a budget alert?
[04:33] Maya: we can set soft budget caps and a hard quota you can opt into. for hosted customers it's per-account; for dedicated we'd do capacity commitments and burn-rate alarms.
[04:46] Rajiv: during the spike did the platform autofallback to smaller model variants?
[04:52] Liam: we didn't see an automated fallback because your routing policy was strict to a single model. we can recommend a fallback chain: primary -> smaller quantized variant -> cached completion fallback, that keeps UX intact while reducing spend under pressure.
[05:10] Sara: good, can we get a proposed fallback chain?
[05:14] Liam: yes. we'll provide a draft policy and sequence.
[05:18] (discussion on who touches SDK and where retry logic lives)
[06:00] Rajiv: our SREs will need a playbook — steps to throttle, to flip on cache-only responses, how to patch retry settings without deployment friction.
[06:12] Priya: Redwood can provide a runbook template and a one-pager for execs on what to expect during a cost incident.
[06:20] Elena: roadmap ask — we need better per-route forecasting and a UI to visualize batch efficiency over time.
[06:28] Maya: that's actually in Redwood Optimize roadmap as predictive batching insights; we'll show you the ETA and put NimbleWorks on the early access list.
[06:38] Tom: timeline on benchmarks and pilot?
[06:42] Liam: recommend a two-week bench window for quant variants: week 1 internal bench + week 2 staged customer pilot in your staging traffic. aiming for mid-March for live pilot.
[06:55] Sara: ok. for internal tasks — i'll share the retry snippet and the traffic schedule for the promo.
[07:02] Maya: perfect. We'll export the cost CSV and the KV hit summary by Tuesday.
[07:10] (silence as folks note next steps)
[07:30] Liam: quick note on long-term levers — model distillation, client-side aggregation, edge batching. these are medium-term but useful to reduce baseline spend.
[07:45] Rajiv: distillation sounds heavy, but edge batching might be quick.
[07:50] Liam: yes; edge batching is a low-friction change: aggregate small short requests at the SDK level for 200-500ms before sending.
[08:02] Elena: any security/compliance concerns with sampling logs we ask Redwood to share?
[08:08] Maya: we'll send sanitized logs and we support KMS-encrypted exports for Private deployments; we'll mark any PII and redact as needed.
[08:18] Tom: can we get a projected cost delta if we implement the batching + retry fixes? even a rough percent helps.
[08:25] Liam: ballpark: fixing retries + batching should reduce token consumption by 30-45% on flash traffic; combined with a quantized pilot you could see 50-70% reduction for those peak flows. we'll back this up with bench numbers.
[08:44] (discussion of scheduling and who does what)
[10:12] Maya: recap — Redwood provides per-route breakdown, alert templates, fallback policy draft, and bench plan. NimbleWorks provides retry code, traffic schedule, and enables sampling.
[10:24] Sara: agreed. action items noted.
[10:30] Maya: ok we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and a shared drive with artifacts. thanks all.
[10:40] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and run-on lines as recorded by auto-transcription. timestamps approximate and provided every 15-120s for context.
